name: Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco
insider_take: Stepping into Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco is like stepping into a living Tuscan fairytale — a fully restored 12th-century medieval borgo nestled within one of Italy's most breathtaking private wine estates.
whats_special: Spread across a staggering 4,200-acre estate in the heart of Montalcino, this is no ordinary luxury resort. Guests enjoy exclusive access to a world-class Brunello di Montalcino DOCG winery, a private Tom Weiskopf-designed 18-hole golf course, and farm-to-table dining sourced directly from the estate's own olive groves and gardens. The borgo itself — with its ancient stone chapel, piazza, and centuries-old towers — creates an atmosphere that no amount of modern design could replicate.
pro_tip: Book a private winery tour and barrel tasting at the estate's Castiglion del Bosco winery. Brunello di Montalcino is one of Italy's most prestigious wines, and drinking it where the grapes were grown is an experience you simply cannot put a price on.
dont_miss: Don't miss a sunset horse ride through the golden Tuscan hills of the estate — the views over the Val d'Orcia, a UNESCO World Heritage landscape, are absolutely unforgettable. Also keep time aside for the Rosewood Spa, which draws on ancient Etruscan wellness traditions using locally sourced herbs and minerals.
pros: Historic 800-year-old Tuscan castle estate with authentic medieval architecture
World-class Brunello di Montalcino vineyard and wine estate on property
Exclusive access to private golf course designed by Tom Fazio
Spacious suites and villas with panoramic views of Val d'Orcia UNESCO landscape
cons: Remote location requires car for exploring nearby towns
Ultra-luxury pricing reflects exclusive estate experience
